Answer: D. Pneumomediastinum, evidenced by linear radiolucencies outlining mediastinal structures.  
Reason: On the PA view (Fig. 5a), there is a thin, sharply demarcated radiolucent line paralleling the left heart border and extending into the superior mediastinum; the lateral view (Fig. 5b) confirms linear lucencies surrounding the trachea and aorta—classic “continuous diaphragm” and “ring-around-the-artery” signs of pneumomediastinum—without mass effect, nodularity, or air-fluid levels.
